title: Take Control of Censoring, Generate Real-World Like Synthetic Data

problem.claim: Benchmarking survival models under varying censoring regimes requires data with realistic and controllable censoring.

contributions.claim: A semi-synthetic framework generates derived survival datasets with an exact user-specified censoring rate among initially uncensored subjects.
The framework evaluates realism using Wasserstein distance and evaluates event–censoring dependence using copula-based Kendall's τ.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Across six public datasets and censoring rates from 10% to 90%, the method better matches the reference distribution and preserves dependence than parametric and random baselines.

narrative_sequence.summary: Survival-model benchmarking needs realistic, controllable censoring.
A semi-synthetic framework controls censoring through covariate-informed subject selection and subject-specific censoring-time sampling.
Realism and event–censoring dependence are assessed with distributional and copula-based measures.
The method reportedly outperforms parametric and random baselines across six datasets and censoring rates from 10% to 90%.

source_observation.claim: The framework separates censoring-rate control from realism assessment and dependence preservation.

interpretation.claim: Synthetic benchmark generation can be made more useful by controlling a target condition while evaluating multiple realism dimensions.

application.claim: Use controllable semi-synthetic data when experiments require systematic variation of censoring conditions.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that the approach generalizes beyond the reported survival-data settings.

unknowns: The six datasets are not identified.
Implementation details and computational costs are not reported.
Statistical significance and uncertainty of the reported comparisons are not reported.
